questions.q: Why isn't deep learning usually the default choice for quantitative finance's typical tabular datasets?
options: Because neural networks cannot be trained on numeric data
Because the usual advantages of deep learning (huge data, raw unstructured inputs, strong signal) don't apply to tabular, low-signal financial data
Because neural networks always perform worse than linear regression
Because financial regulators ban the use of neural networks
questions.explain: Financial data is typically already feature-engineered (not raw pixels/text), has a smaller effective sample size due to overlapping labels, and carries very faint signal -- conditions where deep learning's usual edge doesn't apply.

questions.q: In what situations does this lesson say neural networks genuinely help in quantitative finance?
options: Never -- they should always be avoided
On large alternative-data sets (e.g., satellite imagery, news text, tick-level data) or as one member of an ensemble
Only when there are fewer than 100 rows of data
Only for options pricing
questions.explain: Deep learning becomes competitive when inputs are closer to its comfort zone -- large, often unstructured alternative-data sets -- or when used as one contributor within an ensemble.

questions.q: What does the `alpha` parameter control in scikit-learn's `MLPRegressor`?
options: The number of hidden layers
An L2 weight-decay penalty that discourages the network from growing large weights to fit noise
The random seed
The activation function
questions.explain: MLPRegressor's `alpha` is an L2 regularization penalty on the network's weights, functioning similarly to Ridge regression's penalty on linear model coefficients.

questions.q: What does setting `early_stopping=True` do in MLPRegressor?
options: It stops training immediately with no model fit
It reserves a slice of training data to monitor validation loss and halts training before the network overfits
It removes the need for a test set entirely
It doubles the learning rate
questions.explain: Early stopping in MLPRegressor monitors validation performance internally and stops training once it plateaus, preventing the network from continuing to fit noise.

questions.q: What is dropout, and where is it more commonly available than in scikit-learn's MLPRegressor?
options: A feature-scaling technique, available only in pandas
Randomly zeroing a fraction of neurons during training to prevent over-reliance on any one; more commonly available in dedicated deep learning frameworks like PyTorch or Keras
A method for detecting look-ahead bias
A way to increase the number of training epochs automatically
questions.explain: Dropout randomly deactivates neurons during training as a regularizer, and is a standard feature in frameworks like PyTorch and Keras, though not implemented in scikit-learn's basic MLPRegressor.
